title: Affine sheafification preserves transposed dual-basis components
statement: Let Y be a scheme, U an affine open, A=Gamma(Y,U), and T the associated sheaf functor followed by restriction along U.isoSpec. Let M,N be A-modules with finite bases bM:I and bN:J, f:N -> M, i:I, j:J. Write eM,eN for the comparisons T(M),T(N) with the free sheaves using basis representations, tildeFinsupp, and restrictFreeIso. Write dM,dN for the comparisons T(Hom(M,A)),T(Hom(N,A)) with the same free sheaves using homLinearEquiv followed by the dual-basis representations. Then the (j,i) component of dM^-1 T(precompose f) dN equals the (i,j) component of eN^-1 T(f) eM as unit-sheaf endomorphisms. These are two maps between free sheaves; no internal sheaf Hom occurs in the assertion.

source.place: Tag 01HV(4)-(5) and functoriality; finite free evaluation calculation in duality.tex, Tag 0BQZ. Explicit matrix-component calculation written by X2 from the definitions.

proof.text: Put a_ij=bM.repr(f(bN(j)))(i). dualBasis_repr and dualBasis_apply show that the j-coordinate of bM.dualBasis(i) precomposed with f is a_ij. Hence the two scalar algebraic components coincide.

The defining colimit comparison tildeFinsupp takes the image of each Finsupp single injection to the corresponding free generator, by coconePointUniqueUpToIso compatibility. The projections follow by finite coproduct extensionality. restrictFreeIso is the restriction-to-pullback natural isomorphism followed by pullbackFreeIso; mapFreeIso generator identities show the analogous inclusion identity and naturality handles each scalar endomorphism. Apply sheafification and restriction to the equal algebraic components and use functoriality of composition. This gives exactly the displayed equality. Empty indices are vacuous; the zero-ring case uses the same calculation.

proof_origin.note: The coordinate isomorphisms are shared named definitions in the underlying sheaf category. The dual coordinate definition uses a fixed classical decidable equality internally. The assertion is the algebraic dual matrix-component step, and uses no internal sheaf Hom. The final naturality theorem combines it with the separately proved free internal-dual component calculation.

lean.statement:
theorem affineBasisDualMatrix_component {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.affineOpens)
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U.1)) {I J : Type u} [Finite I] [Finite J]
    [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq J]
    (bM : Basis I Γ(Y, U.1) M) (bN : Basis J Γ(Y, U.1) N) (f : N ⟶ M)
    (i : I) (j : J) :
    let S := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ S
    let eM := affineBasisCoordinatesIso U M bM
    let eN := affineBasisCoordinatesIso U N bN
    let dM := affineDualBasisCoordinatesIso U M bM
    let dN := affineDualBasisCoordinatesIso U N bN
    SheafOfModules.ιFree i ≫ dM.inv ≫
        T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.leftComp Γ(Y, U.1)
          (ModuleCat.of Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(Y, U.1)) f)) ≫ dN.hom ≫ Scheme.Modules.freeπ j =
      SheafOfModules.ιFree j ≫ eN.inv ≫ T.map f ≫ eM.hom ≫ Scheme.Modules.freeπ i
